refuted_findings.description: The 'TaskOutput hook runs because a background shell or task writes' bullet (L67) and the 'What it cannot see' bullet (L72-77) appear to disagree on whether a run_in_background Bash shell's output read via TaskOutput is ever caught: L67 implies yes, L72-77's enumeration attaches the 'unless read through TaskOutput' exception only to subagent writes, not to background-shell writes.
refuted_findings.refutation: Read in context, Passage B's 'read through Read or never' is the exhaustive enumeration of the routes by which background-shell output evades the check, precisely because TaskOutput was just established one sentence earlier (Passage A) as the route that IS caught -- so its omission from the 'cannot see' list is deliberate, not an oversight. docs/09-decisions.md's Ceilings paragraph, edited in the same commit, states the identical logic explicitly for both the run_in_background Bash case and the subagent case ('unless its output is read through TaskOutput, which the wiring catches... The same holds for a subagent'), and the commit message confirms the author deliberately aligned docs/03's phrasing with decision 63's. No genuine inconsistency.

refuted_findings.description: Decision 63's Ceilings paragraph states a run_in_background Bash call's output IS caught when read through TaskOutput, which was flagged as contradicting docs/03-profiles.md's 'What it cannot see' bullet that lists background-shell output as uncaught via Read or never, with no TaskOutput exception offered.
refuted_findings.refutation: This is the same root observation as the docs/03-profiles.md:67-77 finding, from the other file's side. decision 63's paragraph is actually the clearer, unambiguous statement of the (correct, self-consistent) logic -- both the run_in_background Bash case and the subagent case are caught only via TaskOutput, otherwise not -- and docs/03-profiles.md's shorter enumeration reaches the same conclusion by omission rather than an explicit exception clause. No contradiction between the two files once Passage A (docs/03-profiles.md L67) is read together with Passage B.
